output:
**What I found:** Your line-limit gate isn't checking anything. Whenever it fails, the script rewrites the baseline to match the current tree, so every new oversized module joins the exception list and the gate goes green again. That is how 17 modules got in over 12 days without anyone deciding to accept them. Stop the script from writing on a red run, and accept only additions a change names one module at a time (the record calls this RATCHET). What decided it: the list grew from 41 to 58 across 34 rewrites, and no commit message mentions an addition.

**Why it matters:** As things stand, green means "the baseline matches the tree", not "no module grew past the limit". The line-limit debt grows with every regeneration and nothing reports it. Once the script stops writing, the gate blocks new violations again. The 17 entries still need an explicit decision so they don't stay as unowned debt.

**Do this first:**
1. Replace the regeneration script with a reconcile step:
   - A module that is new or bigger, and that the change doesn't name with `--accept-growth <path>`, fails the gate and nothing is written.
   - A module that shrank lowers its entry automatically.
   - A module that is now under the limit is removed.
   - Commit a unit test where an unnamed new module must fail. That test is the gate's proof that it can go red.

Follow-ups:
- Make one commit that lists every entry added since the 41-entry version. For each one, either name it with an owner and a reason, or split the module and drop the entry.
- Give the baseline file an owner (for example via CODEOWNERS), so a diff that adds an entry without naming it is rejected in review.

**What I did not check:** This directory has no git repo and no gate code, so all of the following are still open:
- **How many modules were actually added.** Net +17 can hide more: modules added while others left the list. Run `git diff <sha-12-days-ago> HEAD -- <baseline>.json`.
- **Which commits did the adding.** Run `git log -p --follow -- <baseline>.json`.
- **Whether the gate covers every source module.** Its file globs and ignores weren't measured, so new directories may be missing. Compare the files the gate sees with the source tree.
- **Whether the gate ever went red.** No failing run is on record; finding one, or adding the test above, closes this.

```text
Gate:         Module line-limit merge gate + JSON exception baseline, runs at merge
Stage:        unplaced (merge gate; stage not verified)
Trigger:      churn
Proof:        UNPROVEN (no recorded red run; every red was converted to green by regeneration)
Scope:        declared all source modules over limit / effective modules not in a baseline that
              tracks the tree / delta: every module that grew past the limit in the window (≥17)
Baseline:     41 → 58 in 12 days, 34 rewrites; last accepted growth: none named
Status:       BLOCKING (nominally; regeneration makes it non-blocking in practice)
Decision:     RATCHET
Guard:        Unnamed growth refused by reconcile; baseline has a named owner; the refused-case
              test runs in CI as the gate's negative control
Handoff:      none (the PROVE condition is met by the refused-case test in the same change)
Next action:  Replace the regeneration script with reconcile (per-entry --accept-growth, red run
              writes nothing, stale entries removed) plus its refused-case test
Verification: Not run — no repository or gate code in the working directory
```
